alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ rendered by the verse-initial For.
Aorist imperative rendered by the bare imperative consider.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun him and nothing else. The ASV writes a second word (that), so the ordinary split applies rather than rule 90's single-relativizer case.
The participle carries the supplied relativizer and auxiliary under rules 7, 9 and 32; head on the lexical verb endured, not on the auxiliary hath.
Attributive demonstrative on the anarthrous ἀντιλογίαν; no article competes, so the ordinary alignment applies.
Noun rendered by a single English noun.
The expressed preposition ὑπό is what the English of answers to under rule 36; the ASV renders agentive ὑπό by of here.
The ASV gives sinners no determiner, so the article has no the to anchor: rule 23. Rule 21 forbids leaving a bare of on it, and the of belongs to the expressed preposition in any case.
Substantival adjective rendered by the bare noun sinners.

The ASV's himself answers to this reflexive pronoun. SBLGNT.HEB.12.3.v001 is marked FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE, the projection carrying the plural base ἑαυτούς while the ASV text renders a singular (its margin notes the plural themselves), but the token itself is present and is what the English realizes, so this is not rule 97's case of English answering to an absent source word; only the number differs. Rule 12 bars making a new textual decision here.
Purpose ἵνα realized by the word introducing the English clause, rule 40; here the ASV writes that rather than an infinitival to.
Ordinary negative μή rendered by not; no negative indefinite stands with it, so rules 41 and 59 do not arise.

The inflected verb takes its supplied subject ye and the copular wax under rules 7 and 9; rule 17 heads the unit on the meaning-bearing weary rather than on the light verb wax, as make straight heads on straight. Discontinuous around not under rule 15.

The genitive pronoun ὑμῶν is present and free to take the supplied possessive your, so rule 20 proper applies and the article realizes nothing. Rule 76's availability test does not save it: ὑμῶν has been spent on no other role.
No Greek preposition is expressed and the article carries no determiner, so the dative's English in stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause; discontinuous around your under rule 15.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive your, rule 20.

review_notes: All 18 source and 21 target ids are partitioned exactly once.
τὸν is split from its participle under rule 32; the article keeps only him and the participle carries that hath endured.
ὑπό keeps the English of under rule 36, leaving τῶν unrepresented under rule 23 rather than handing it a bare of, which rule 21 forbids.

s010 is aligned despite the FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE marking: the token is present in the projection and the ASV's himself answers to it, only the number differing, so rule 97 does not apply and rule 12 bars a fresh textual decision.
κάμητε heads on weary rather than the light verb wax, per rule 17.
